newsitem.title: IRAN: Qatari minister says Iran vital to Gulf security.
newsitem.headline: Qatari minister says Iran vital to Gulf security.

text.p: Qatar's Foreign Minister Sheikh Hamad bin Jassim bin Jabr al-Thani said Iran was important in maintaining peace and security in the oil-rich Gulf region, the official Iranian news agency IRNA reported on Saturday.
"Qatar attaches high importance on Iran's principled efforts to develop peace and security in the sensitive and strategic region," Sheikh Hamad was quote by IRNA as saying.
It said Sheikh Hamad, who arrived in Tehran earlier on Saturday for a one-day visit, was speaking at a meeting with Iran's President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani.
He was quoted as saying that Qatar saw Iran's peace efforts in the Gulf as "effective in stopping foreign intervention in the region."
IRNA quoted Rafsanjani as saying that Iran was ready to offer economic, industrial and technical assistance to neighbouring Gulf states.
Iran, whose influence in the region diminished after the 1979 fall of the late Shah, has been trying to improve ties with Qatar and other Gulf Arab states.
Qatar, a small oil and gas-rich country, maintains close political and economic relations with Iran.
In May Qatar politely declined an Iranian offer of a defence pact, saying it was not necessary at this stage.

Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states have repeatedly accused Iran of posing a threat to the security of the region, which has about half of the world's proven oil reserves. They have also expressed concern over Iran's armament programmes saying it exceeded its conventional defensive needs.
The GCC groups Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain and Oman.

A GCC summit in Doha in December called on Iran to end its occupation of three Gulf islands claimed by the United Arab Emirates, and criticised its deployment of surface-to-surface missiles in the region.
